title: Social Stratification and Role Conflict
text:
Social stratification refers to the system by which a society ranks categories of people into a hierarchy. This arrangement determines access to resources, power, and social privilege across different groups. It is not merely about individual wealth but reflects ingrained structural inequalities that persist through generations.

Within this framework, role conflict emerges when an individual occupies multiple positions or roles whose expectations contradict one another. For instance, the pressure to be both a committed employee and a primary caregiver can create significant psychological strain, as the demands of each role pull the person in opposing directions.

Sociological analysis suggests that institutionalization often reinforces these conflicts, creating powerful social scripts that dictate acceptable behavior even when personal needs diverge from prescribed roles. Understanding this tension is crucial for analyzing systemic pressure points within family and professional life.
